result:
- **The change is recorded in history.** Commit `546dc8b` ("🔒 Update login.py to receive password as body (#33)", 2019-05-28) changed `new_password` from a query parameter to a body parameter. I confirmed this with `git show 546dc8b`.
- **The stated reason is security.** The commit message says "for security". It points to a StackOverflow answer on whether query-string parameters are secure over HTTPS (`https://stackoverflow.com/questions/2629222/are-querystring-parameters-secure-in-https-http-ssl`). I did not fetch that link, so I can't say what it argues. The message doesn't spell out the specific risk. It is likely about URLs being logged or exposed, but that is my inference and not stated in the repo.
- **The current code still works this way.** `reset_password(session: SessionDep, body: NewPassword)` is at `backend/app/api/routes/login.py:78`. The `NewPassword` model is at `backend/app/models.py:131`. The route is `@router.post("/reset-password/")` at `login.py:77`.
- **The token goes in the URL, as it always has.** The reset email link is `{FRONTEND_HOST}/reset-password?token={token}` (`backend/app/utils.py:72`). So the commit moved only the password out of the URL. The token still travels there.
- **Other reasons are unknown.** I found no design doc or comment beyond that commit message. I searched `backend/app` for "reset.password" and "NewPassword", and ran `git show` on the commit.
